1	# Testing
2	
3	Read this **before writing or modifying any test** under `src/test/java/`.
4	
5	## Two test layers — the class suffix picks the Maven phase
6	
7	| Layer                 | Suffix  | Runs in         | Framework                                              | Skill                               |
8	|-----------------------|---------|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
9	| Server-side view test | `*Test` | `./mvnw test`   | Vaadin Browserless (`SpringBrowserlessTest`)           | `aiup-vaadin-jooq:browserless-test` |
10	| Browser test          | `*IT`   | `./mvnw verify` | Playwright + Drama Finder (`AbstractBasePlaywrightIT`) | `aiup-vaadin-jooq:playwright-test`  |
11	
12	Surefire picks up `*Test`, Failsafe picks up `*IT` (both configured via `spring-boot-starter-parent`; the failsafe
13	plugin is declared in `pom.xml`). A browserless test named `*IT` or a Playwright test named `*Test` runs in the wrong
14	phase, and `TestLayerConventionsTest` fails the build when one does. The rule is worth enforcing because the
15	failure is otherwise silent: nothing errors, the wrong Maven plugin simply never picks the class up, and a test
16	that never runs reports as passing. Browserless is the default for use cases; Playwright is for test cases (`TC-*`) and
17	anything that genuinely needs a browser (client-side rendering, keyboard focus, scrolling).
18	
19	## Framework
20	
21	- **Vaadin Browserless Testing** (`browserless-test-junit6` + `browserless-test-spring`) is the default for Vaadin view
22	  tests — server-side, no
23	  browser, no servlet container.
24	  Reference: https://vaadin.com/docs/latest/flow/testing/browserless/getting-started
25	- View tests extend `PetClinicTestBase` (or `SpringBrowserlessTest` directly for tests that don't touch the DB, in
26	  which case add `@SpringBootTest` and `@Import(TestcontainersConfiguration.class)` yourself).
27	  They run inside a Spring context and use the same Testcontainers Postgres as the rest of the tests.
28	- **Use the `aiup-vaadin-jooq:browserless-test` skill** to scaffold a browserless test for a use case. Prefer it over
29	  hand-rolling — it knows the conventions in this file (locators, `@UseCase`, naming, etc.).
30	- **Karibu is gone.** Any `com.github.mvysny.kaributesting.*` import is a mistake — the project is all
31	  `SpringBrowserlessTest` / `ComponentQuery` now. The `karibu-test` skill is obsolete.
32	
33	## Test class naming — `UC<NNN><UseCaseName>Test`
34	
35	Tests that verify a use case are named after the use case, **not** the view. Format:
36	`UC<NNN><UseCaseNameInPascalCase>Test`, e.g `UC001ViewWelcomePageTest`, `UC004FindOwnersByLastNameTest`,
37	`UC007AddPetToOwnerTest`. The `NNN` matches the `UC-NNN-*.md` file in `docs/use_cases/`.
38	
39	If a view is touched by multiple use cases, write one `UC<NNN>…Test` class per use case rather than one `XxxViewTest`
40	covering all of them. Keep the test file in the **same package as the view under test** and name the class after the UC.
41	
42	**Exception — cross-cutting tests.** `ArchitectureTest` (the ArchUnit rules behind
43	[`development.md`](development.md)) and `PetclinicApplicationTests` verify no single use case, so they sit in the
44	root package under their own names. Everything that *does* verify a use case follows the format above.
45	
46	## `@UseCase` on every test method
47	
48	Every `@Test` method that verifies UC behaviour must carry `ai.unifiedprocess.petclinic.UseCase` **on the method**
49	(never on the class — the annotation is `@Target(METHOD)` and cannot go on a class):
50	
51	```java
52	@Test
53	@UseCase(id = "UC-004", scenario = "A2: Exactly One Match", businessRules = "BR-001")
54	void exactlyOneMatchNavigatesDirectlyToOwnerDetails() { ... }
55	```
56	
57	- `id` — required, matches a `docs/use_cases/UC-NNN-*.md` file.
58	- `scenario` — optional, defaults to `"Main Success Scenario"`. Set it for alternative flow

3	Rules that more than one use case must honour.
4	
5	A rule that belongs to a single use case stays **in** that use case as
6	`BR-NNN` — it is part of that use case's story and has no life of its own. A
7	rule that several use cases share lives **here** as `GR-NNN`, is stated once,
8	and is referenced by each use case that applies it. The use case keeps its local
9	`BR-NNN` heading, so tests and the traceability sensors still point at a rule of
10	that use case; the heading says which shared rule it realizes instead of
11	restating it.
12	
13	`BusinessRuleTraceabilityTest` (`./mvnw test`) keeps the two sides honest: it
14	fails when a use case references a rule that does not exist, when a link lands
15	on a renamed heading, when the `**Realized by:**` line and the use cases
16	disagree in either direction, when the summary table drifts from the rules below
17	it, or when a rule here is realized by fewer than two use cases.
18	
19	**Why `GR` and not `BR`.** `BR-NNN` ids are scoped to a use case: every
20	`UC-NNN-*.md` numbers its rules from `BR-001`, and `@UseCase(businessRules =

trajectory.message:
I've written UC-002, but none of it has been compiled or run. This environment has no Docker and Maven can't resolve its plugins offline, so even the sensor run (`./mvnw -q test -Dgroups=sensor`) failed to start. Please run `./mvnw test` on a machine with Docker. That also regenerates the jOOQ sources, and I referenced their `Tables.*` constants without seeing them generated.

**What I added**
- **`vet/domain/Vet.java`:** a serializable record holding id, first name, last name and a list of specialties.
- **`vet/domain/VetRepository.java`:** `findPage(offset, limit)` and `count()`.
  - The specialties come from a jOOQ `multiset` in the same query, so there's no N+1.
  - Specialties are ordered alphabetically (BR-002).
  - Vets are ordered by last name, first name, then id.
  - The class is `@Repository` and read-only transactional.
- **`vet/ui/VetsView.java`:** a route at `vets` inside `MainLayout`.
  - It has a grid with First Name, Last Name and Specialties columns.
  - Specialties are comma-separated, or "none" when a vet has none.
  - The grid loads lazily through callback fetch and count (BR-001).
  - There's no authentication (BR-003).
  - The repository field is `transient` and the lambdas read it through `this.repository`, as the conventions require.
- **`MainLayout`:** the "Veterinarians" nav item now points at `VetsView.class` instead of a path string.
- **`UC002ViewVeterinariansTest`:** covers the main scenario, BR-001 to BR-003, the "none" rendering, and A1 (no vets).

**Open items**
- I left `Status: Approved` as it is. Setting `Done` needs the `aiup-vaadin-jooq:coverage-check` audit first, and the hooks refuse the change without it.
- The tests don't exercise scrolling to fetch further chunks. The seed data has only six vets, which is under one fetch chunk. A Playwright `*IT` would be needed for that.
